title: Platform systems & services: playbook, runbooks, dashboards, and roadmap
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Consolidated platform playbook for systems & services: inventories, common how-tos, dashboard and alert definitions, runbooks for common incidents, retrospective learnings, and the near-term roadmap. This doc is the canonical starting point for platform engineers and oncall responders.
body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook captures the operational model for Redwood's platform systems and services maintained by the Platform team. It centralizes: the service inventory, standard how-tos, dashboard and alert definitions, runbooks for common incidents, retrospective learnings, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended for platform engineers, oncall, and SRE partners.

Scope
- Applies to the components listed in the Systems & Services Inventory section (control plane services, observability, CI/CD, infra automation, and core shared services).
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks linked in related_pages; it provides cross-cutting patterns and references.

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-platform (Platform systems & services)
- Oncall rotation: platform-oncall (PagerDuty team: PLAT-ONCALL)
- Escalation path:
  1) Primary oncall -> 2) Platform oncall secondary -> 3) Platform tech lead -> 4) Eng SRE manager
- Primary contacts:
  - Pager duty: platform-oncall
  - Slack channel: #platform-ops
  - Email: platform@redwood.com

Systems & Services Inventory (short)
Use this as the canonical short inventory—service owners must maintain links in their service pages.

- control-plane-api (owner: platform/control-plane) — auth, routing, model-routing policy engine, API gateway
- runtime-scheduler (owner: platform/runtime) — GPU scheduling, continuous batching coordinator
- kv-cache-service (owner: platform/runtime) — prefix/KV caching and cache invalidation API
- metrics-ingest (owner: infra/observability) — metrics collection pipeline (Prometheus remote_write -> Cortex)
- logs-ingest (owner: infra/observability) — log collection (Fluentd -> Loki)
- ci-cd (owner: infra/ci) — build pipelines, image registry, canary deploy tooling
- infra-provisioner (owner: infra/iac) — Terraform orchestrator, state storage, bootstrapping scripts
- secrets-kms-proxy (owner: security) — KMS proxy for private deployments
- deployment-console (owner: product/console) — internal platform console used by SREs and account teams

Service metadata table (text)
Service | Owner | Primary SLO | PagerDuty team
control-plane-api | platform/control-plane | p99 latency < 150ms for control plane ops | PLAT-API
runtime-scheduler | platform/runtime | scheduling latency p95 < 200ms, scheduling error rate < 0.5% | PLAT-RUNTIME
metrics-ingest | infra/observability | data availability 99.9% (24h) | OBS-INGEST

How-tos (common tasks)
- Adding a new Grafana dashboard
  1) Fork dashboards repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood/platform-dashboards.git
  2) Add a JSON panel and follow naming conventions: dashboards/platform/<service-name>/<dashboard-name>.json
  3) Run local validation: ./scripts/validate-dashboard.sh <file>
  4) Open PR and request reviewers: @platform-observability, @service-owner
  5) On merge, CI will push to Grafana provisioning.

- Adding an alert rule
  1) Open an RFC in the platform issue tracker describing symptom, target SLO, and suggested thresholds.
  2) Implement rule in alerts/ directory and include runbook_id in the alert annotation. Example alert annotation: runbook_id=plat-runtime-high-p99-latency
  3) Add to alerting policy and run CI tests: ./scripts/test-alerts.sh
  4) Deploy via terraform apply -target=module.alerting
  5) Verify firing/resolve behavior in staging Grafana Alerts UI.

- Performing a controlled canary deploy for control-plane-api
  1) Create a new canary image tag and update the canary k8s manifest in ci-cd/canaries/.
  2) Trigger the canary pipeline: make canary-deploy SERVICE=control-plane-api TAG=<tag>
  3) Monitor the canary dashboard (control-plane-api/canary) and key SLOs for 30 minutes.
  4) If metrics OK (no >1% increase in error rate, p99 latency within 10% of baseline), promote to progressive rollout.
  5) If metrics break, rollback: make rollback SERVICE=control-plane-api CANARY=true and open postmortem ticket.

Dashboards & Alerts catalog (high level)
- Dashboard naming convention: <team>/<service>/<purpose> (e.g. platform/control-plane-api/production-overview)
- Canonical dashboards to review on incidents:
  - platform/control-plane-api/production-overview — traffic, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token-rate by route
  - platform/runtime/serving-health — GPU utilization, queue length, scheduling latency, batch sizes, memory pressure, kv-cache hit rate
  - infra/observability/ingest-pipeline — write latency, scrape lag, retention pressure, Cortex ingesters healthy
  - infra/ci/pipeline-health — recent failures, mean time to green, flaky test rate

Alerting thresholds (examples)
- control-plane-api p99 latency > 250ms for 5m -> Severity P1 (pager)
- control-plane-api error rate > 1.5% for 5m -> Severity P1 (pager)
- runtime-scheduler scheduling error rate > 1% for 10m -> Severity P1 (pager)
- runtime-scheduler GPU utilization > 92% sustained for 15m -> Severity P2 (page + slack)
- kv-cache hit rate drop > 10 percentage points vs baseline for 10m -> Severity P2
- metrics-ingest missing 5% of expected metrics in 24h -> Severity P2
- Node pool autoscaler unable to scale (failed scaling ops) for 30m -> Severity P1

Runbooks (quick links and canonical steps)
- platform/control-plane-api: runbook_id=plat-controlplane-api-incident
  1) Triage: identify whether incident is control-plane-only (admin API) or ingress (customer traffic).
  2) If ingress, verify routing changes and fallback model variants using routing policy UI.
  3) Check API gateway errors and upstream control-plane pods: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=control-plane-api
  4) Collect traces: open traces in Tempo using trace_id from request headers.
  5) If degraded and not recoverable in 10m, redirect traffic to standby region following failover runbook.
  6) Declare incident, capture timeline, and assign postmortem owner.

- platform/runtime scheduling backlog: runbook_id=plat-runtime-backlog
  1) Inspect scheduler metrics: queue length, average scheduling latency, pending pods, GPU allocation failures.
  2) If queue length high and GPU utilization < 85%, investigate pod throttling and preemption logs.
  3) If GPU utilization > 95%, trigger burst capacity policy: scale out reserved GPU pool (see infra-provisioner runbook).
  4) If KV cache hit rate low, consider invalidation storm or cache eviction; check kv-cache logs and recent deployments.

Post-incident retrospective guidance (how we run brief retros)
- When to run: any P1 or repeated P2 within the same week; otherwise quarterly review for systemic issues.
- Structure: 1) Timeline & facts, 2) Root cause analysis, 3) Actions (owners + due dates), 4) Metrics to validate remediation (what's success).
- Templates: use retro template at confluence/eng-platform/retrospective-template
- Typical corrective actions observed in past retros:
  - Improve observability for scheduling (additional histograms for batch sizes)
  - Harden autoscaler failure modes (retry & circuit-breakers)
  - Add chaos tests for cluster capacity exhaustion

Recent retrospectives (examples)
- Q4 2025: Runtime scheduling backlog incident — root cause: scheduler heap growth under certain model multiplexing patterns. Actions: patch scheduler GC, add a p95 memory alert, additional unit/integration tests.
- Q1 2026: Control-plane API increased p99 latency during canaries — root cause: shared connection pool exhaustion to model routing DB. Actions: connection pool sizing, add circuit-breaker, extend canary observation window.

Roadmap (next 3 quarters)
- Q2 2026:
  - Deliver global dashboard UI improvements: unified incident timeline + traces with metrics correlation (owner: infra/observability)
  - Complete first-pass autoscaler resiliency work (owner: eng-sre + infra/iac)
  - Standardize runbook annotations on all alerts (owner: platform)
- Q3 2026:
  - Launch platform capacity forecasting tool (ML-based forecast for GPU usage) (owner: platform/forecasting)
  - Deploy canary gating automation: failed canaries block progressive rollout automatically (owner: ci-cd)
  - Expand KV cache to support multi-tenant eviction policies (owner: platform/runtime)
- Q4 2026:
  - Private deployment ops kit (onprem packaging improvements + compliance playbook) (owner: eng-private-deployments)
  - Cost-optimization initiative: adaptive batching recommendations surfaced in console (owner: optimize)

Team wiki and onboarding pointers
- New engineers: start with the platform team wiki index: confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki-index
- Oncall runbook walkthrough: schedule a 1:1 shadow with current oncall for first rotation
- Useful repos:
  - git@github.com:redwood/platform-dashboards.git
  - git@github.com:redwood/platform-runbooks.git
  - git@github.com:redwood/infra-terraform.git

Appendices
- SLOs and error budgets (summary)
  - control-plane-api: availability 99.95% monthly, latency p99 < 150ms internal control ops
  - runtime-serving: throughput SLO per GPU, scheduling latency p95 < 200ms
- Runbook ownership expectations
  - Every service must have a runbook with: detection steps, mitigation steps, rollback, remediation actions, and a postmortem link.

Revision history
- 2025-10-15 created by Aisha Patel
- 2025-12-10 update: added runtime backlog runbook (reviewers: Marco Diaz)
- 2026-01-18 update: standardized alert annotations and added canary guidance
- 2026-02-20 update: roadmap refresh and retrospective summaries (last_updated by Priya Shah)

Where to go next
- If you are a service owner and do not have a page linked from the inventory above, create one and add it to related_pages.
- For platform-wide changes, open a Platform RFC and tag the reviewers listed in this document.
